newsitem.title: CHILE: RTRS-Chile's Escondida close fo signing finance deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Chile's Escondida close fo signing finance deal.

text.p: Chile's giant Escondida copper mine, 57.5 percent owned by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, is close to a deal with a syndicate of banks for a loan to finance projects including a $460 million oxides plant, said the pit's technical manager David Borries.
"Escondida has already negotiated a certain amount of money from a syndicate of banks. It's just about tied up," Borries told reporters at a copper conference in Santiago.
"We've had some pretty good offers," he said.
Borries declined to give further details of the loan.
Construction of the 125,000-tonne oxide heap-leaching plant will start in April with the first cathode expected to be cast in August 1998.
Although the plant is designed to produce 125,000 tonnes of copper cathodes a year, output could be boosted to 139,000 tonnes to take advantage of high early ore grades, he said.
"We could run it at 139,000 tonnes if we turn up the amps which is quite possible," said Borries, adding, "The higher ore grades in the initial oxide years may allow us to do this."
Escondida may expand the plant in 2003-4 to treat oxides from the Escondida North deposit which will come into production in 2001, said Borries.
Escondida North contains 70 million tonnes of oxide ores which are not sufficient to justify building a second pant, he said.
"You would never develop it as an oxide mine in its own right," said Borries.
"In 2003-4 there is no reason why we should not build phase two in the oxides plant to take it up to whatever we consider as the right size for the ore available."
